Subject: Re: Post-call: Amaya security & data retention follow-up — answers and SLA summary

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear asks, Alex — and thanks Marissa for routing. Below is a concise set of answers we can include in the questionnaire and call out in the vendor pack. I've also attached a brief data-retention-sla-summary.pdf that you can share with procurement.

1) SOC 2:
- Current status: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I in 2026 and the Type II audit is in progress. We expect the Type II report to be available by 2027-06-15. We can provide the Type I report now and provide a redacted Type II report once finalized (standard NDA/controls redaction).

2) GDPR / Data subject requests (DSRs):
- Data export & deletion: We support data export and deletion APIs. Deletion requests are processed and data removed from primary storage within 30 days by default (measured from request acknowledgement).

3) Backups & snapshots:
- Immutable backups / snapshot windows: For hosted customers, encrypted backups and cross-region snapshots are retained for up to 90 days by default due to snapshot lifecycle and restore guarantees. During that period, copies may exist in encrypted snapshots; however, backups are inaccessible for serving after primary deletion. For Dedicated/Private deployments, we can negotiate shorter backup retention windows in the contract (and support on-prem snapshots where you control retention).

4) Logs retention and purge:
- Standard logging: Request traces and operational logs are retained 180 days by default.
- Per-customer purge: We support scoped log redaction and targeted purges for most logs; the purge operation timeline depends on log store replication windows but typically completes within 7-14 days. For strict requirements we recommend Private deployments where logs live in customer-controlled storage.

5) HIPAA / BAA:
- BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for customers on Private deployments and for certain Dedicated engagements where controls and network isolation meet HIPAA requirements. For hosted customers we evaluate on a case-by-case basis; please flag any required covered workloads and we'll provide the checklist.

6) Key management & encryption:
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can opt into provider-managed encryption with role-based access and logging.

7) What we can commit to in the procurement pack:
- We can commit to a 30-day primary deletion SLA, document backup retention windows (90 days default for hosted), and log retention (180 days default), with contract-level options to tighten those windows for Dedicated/Private customers. We will also include our SOC 2 Type I report and target date for Type II.

Next steps I recommend:
- Marissa: share the attached data-retention-sla-summary.pdf + SOC 2 Type I with Alex and procurement.
- If Amaya needs accelerated deletion guarantees for backups/logs, let's schedule a quick tech call (Rishi + Neha + Alex) to scope the Dedicated/Private options.

If that looks good, Marissa — I'll start populating the questionnaire directly and mark fields where commercial negotiation is required.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachment: data-retention-sla-summary.pdf
